Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a sharply demarcated, thin-walled cystic cavity with an air-fluid level in the left lower lobe, which is a classic radiographic appearance of intralobar pulmonary sequestration. This congenital malformation predisposes patients to recurrent pulmonary infections and fits the clinical history better than emphysema (which presents as hyperlucency), tuberculosis (typically apical/thick-walled), or heart failure (bilateral edema).
